Feature Importance Insights

  • Feature importance varies by model type and evaluation method
  • Random Forest provides intrinsic feature importance scores based on impurity reduction
  • Mutual information identifies features with strong non-linear relationships to the target
  • ANOVA F-values measure linear relationships between features and target
  • PCA analysis reveals feature redundancy and helps with dimensionality reduction

Next Steps for Feature Engineering

  • Remove redundant features: Consider dropping highly correlated features to reduce dimensionality
  • Focus on top features: Build simpler models using only the most important features
  • Explore interactions: Create interaction terms between top features
  • Dimensionality reduction: Use PCA or other methods to create new feature representations
  • Feature selection: Use recursive feature elimination or other selection methods

Dataset Information

ML Pipeline Overview

Croissant Dataset → Feature Extraction → Preprocessing → 
ClusterID-aware CV → Model Training → Evaluation → Visualization

Key Pipeline Components

Component Purpose Implementation
CroissantLoader Load and parse Croissant-formatted dataset Extracts features, labels, ClusterIDs
FeatureProcessor Clean and preprocess features Handles missing values, categorical encoding
FeatureEvaluator Analyze feature importance and relationships Correlation, ANOVA, mutual information, PCA
ClusterAwareCV Prevent data leakage Ensures same-cluster samples stay together
ModelTrainer Train multiple ML models Random Forest, SVM, Logistic Regression
Evaluator Comprehensive model evaluation Multiple metrics, visualizations, statistical tests

Methodology Notes

  • ClusterID-aware cross-validation: Prevents data leakage by ensuring all interfaces from the same sequence cluster stay together in training or testing sets
  • Feature evaluation: Comprehensive analysis including correlation, ANOVA, mutual information, and PCA
  • Stratified sampling: Maintains class balance across folds
  • Multiple metrics: Evaluates models using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and ROC-AUC
  • Feature scaling: All features standardized for distance-based algorithms
  • Model diversity: Includes tree-based, linear, and kernel-based models
